decisions.decision: Downgraded from supported to unresolved; derivation changed from explicit to inferred with stated premises; evidence reduced to context only.
decisions.rationale: No inspected OpenAI text names the December 2023 Beta as the edition Version 2 replaces. Searched: the April 2025 update page (live and 2025-04-16 capture), the Version 2 PDF (all pages, including section 1.1 and the change log), the Frontier Governance Framework PDF and release page, OpenAI’s safety pages (the former preparedness URL now redirects to the general safety page) and the o3/o4-mini system card, which calls itself the first launch under the updated framework without naming the earlier edition. Secondary accounts that describe a replacement are not publisher documentation. The overstated paraphrase (an update to a framework first released in 2023) was replaced by a verbatim context quote.

time.note: Cover last-updated date and dated publication announcement both identify April 15, 2025; no distinct effective date is asserted.

claim.qualification: This records replacement in the public policy version sequence, supported by the publisher’s update history. It does not retire historical claims or prove implementation.

claim.subject: preparedness-v2
claim.statement: Preparedness Framework Version 2 replaces Beta in the publisher’s documented framework version sequence.

time.note: Cover last-updated date and dated publication announcement both identify April 15, 2025; no distinct effective date is asserted.

claim.qualification: Unresolved. The publisher’s update page and the Version 2 change log describe an update without naming the edition updated; secondary accounts that describe a replacement are not publisher documentation. Downgraded on 2026-10-03 from supported, which rested on an overstated paraphrase. It does not retire historical claims or prove implementation.
claim.inferenceRationale: Premises: OpenAI calls the April 2025 document an update to its Preparedness Framework; the Version 2 change log lists changes made in that version, including removal of the low and medium levels that the December 2023 Beta used; the Beta is the only earlier edition identified. These make replacement plausible, but no inspected OpenAI text names the Beta as the edition Version 2 replaces, so the replacement is not established as publisher-documented.

decisions.decision: Requalified: statement and qualification now follow the source (designed in the spirit of the framework being developed by Christiano and ARC Evals); evidence became the verbatim whole sentence. ID and explicitly_credits relation kept.
decisions.rationale: explicitly_credits covers an express attribution of intellectual contribution with the scope retained in the claim. The sentence expressly attributes development of the RSP framework to Christiano and ARC Evals and scopes the relation as “in the spirit of”, alongside government proposals; the narrower scope is now in the statement and qualification rather than implied by “credits”.

claim.subject: rsp-2023
claim.statement: Anthropic RSP v1.0 says its commitments are designed in the spirit of the Responsible Scaling Policy framework being developed by Paul Christiano and ARC Evals.
claim.qualification: Scoped attribution: the policy names Christiano, with ARC Evals, as developing the RSP framework and says its commitments are designed in that framework’s spirit, alongside emerging government proposals. It does not say the commitments were derived from, adopted from or endorsed by Christiano; the paragraph’s explicit thanks go to ARC Evals only. Not sole authorship or proof that every commitment was implemented. Requalified on 2026-10-03 from “credits a framework”. Distinct from rsp-credits-arc-2023.
